question: Using the definition of ADS and Table 5A-1, explain why Level 2 is not an ADS level while Level 3 is.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD defines an Automated Driving System (ADS) as hardware and software capable of performing the *entire* Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, a term applied specifically to Levels 3, 4, and 5. Level 2 does not qualify because, per Table 5A-1, it executes only steering and acceleration/deceleration while "the human driver performs all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task" — so the system performs only part of the DDT and falls in the ADAS category. Level 3, by contrast, is "sustained performance by an ADS of all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD," satisfying the full-DDT criterion (the human is only expected to respond to a request to intervene), so it is classed as ADS. Standards (mandatory): - The acronym is formally established: "ADS-Automated Driving System" (among the acronyms that "shall have the following meanings"). Support (informational): - "Automated Driving System (ADS) - The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing the entire Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, regardless of whether it is limited to a specific Operational Design Domain (ODD); this term is used specifically to describe a Level 3, 4, or 5 driving automation system." - The broader term "Driving Automation System" covers systems performing "part or all of the DDT on a sustained basis" (Levels 1–5), which is why Level 2 is still a driving automation system but not an ADS. - Table 5A-1 assigns Levels 1–2 to the "Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)" category and Levels 3–5 to the "Automated Driving System (ADS)" category; Level 2's description expressly leaves remaining DDT aspects to the human driver, while Level 3's description covers "all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 5A-1 shows the "Automation Category" column grouping Levels 1–2 under ADAS and Levels 3–5 under ADS, with Level 2's description requiring the human driver to perform all remaining DDT aspects and Level 3's covering all aspects of the DDT. [Image 2] The full page shows both the definitions list (including the ADS definition in Item B) and Table 5A-1 confirming the Level 2/ADAS vs. Level 3/ADS split. [Image 4] The page presents Part 5's general overview and the definitions section (5A.03) that anchors the ADS/ADAS distinction. Citations: - Section 5A.03 Support §1 (p.760) - Table 5A-1 (p.760) - Section 1C.03 Standard §1 (p.31) - Section 5A.02 Support §1 (p.759)
gold_answer: An ADS performs the entire dynamic driving task on a sustained basis and the term applies to Levels 3-5. Level 2 performs steering and acceleration/deceleration but still expects the human to perform all remaining aspects of the task, so it is ADAS rather than ADS. Level 3 performs all aspects within its ODD, subject to a human fallback request.
